title: Bad Drives Out Good
equation: Adverse Selection = Quality Opacity × Price Rigidity
hook: You're doing better work than the cheap guys, but customers can't tell the difference.
statement: When buyers can't see quality and the price can't move, the cheap stuff pushes out the good stuff.
explainer: If everyone pays the same and nobody can spot the difference upfront, your extra effort goes unpaid. Good sellers quit, and the market fills up with cheaper fakes.
sop: Find where you sell at a set price and buyers can't check quality first.
Multiply them to see how exposed you are.
Make quality visible with proof, guarantees, reviews, and transparency.
equation_example: Quality Opacity 8 × Price Rigidity 7 = 56 out of 100. High means buyers can't tell good from bad at a fixed price, so quality sellers leave. Low means quality can still earn its price.
question: Write down one way you could prove your quality to a buyer before they pay.
closing_statement: If quality's hidden, make yours impossible to fake.
caption:
Principle Nº 341: Bad Drives Out Good

You're doing better work than the cheap guys, but customers can't tell the difference.

When buyers can't see quality and the price can't move, the cheap stuff pushes out the good stuff.

Your turn: Write down one way you could prove your quality to a buyer before they pay.
